inlineContent.text: iOS suspends an app soon after it leaves the foreground, and with it the Bluetooth tag the
device broadcasts: the BlueGPS antennas lose the device. A
keeps it running. It shows your Live Activity for something the user started, such as a

the tag advertisement keeps going;
your code keeps running, and the content you send reaches the Live Activity;
the session reports what it runs without, and every time the app was suspended anyway.
What the Live Activity shows is yours: its type, its content, its layout and its
actions. The session requests it, carries your content to it and ends it; it adds
nothing of its own.
It needs three things working together: tag advertising, the two Bluetooth background
modes and a Live Activity. Take any of them away and the app is suspended in the
background as usual.

content.text: What to evaluate for your deployment

inlineContent.text: The session runs within limits set by iOS and by App Review. The SDK reports what it can
observe; whether each limit is acceptable for your app is yours to decide.
App Review
The Live Activity must show something the user started and follows, such as a navigation, and end with it. Justify the two Bluetooth background modes by the positioning they serve.
Display off

Apple describes the display turning off as the end of the Live Activity’s Bluetooth privilege for scanning. With current iOS versions the app keeps running with the display off: scanning slows down, advertising goes on. Behaviour can change with iOS releases: watch
and
to know whether it holds on your users’ devices.
Brief suspensions
The app can be suspended for a few seconds when the device is locked again shortly after being unlocked. Your code resumes afterwards; design it to tolerate such pauses.
Battery
Keeping the radio advertising and the app running costs energy. Measure it on your devices, for the session lengths you expect.
The system ends a Live Activity after eight hours at most. The session reports
and goes on, but without a Live Activity the app falls back to the usual background limits. A new Live Activity needs the app in the foreground.
